s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent palpitations with wide complex tachycardia and abnormal cardiac structure
salient_findings: Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
Grossly dilated RV with high RV end diastolic volume
key_facts: Male patient in his 20s
Complaints of intermittent palpitations for 2 days
Worsening of palpitations in the previous hour
No history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
No past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
Respiratory rate was 14 bpm
ECG showed wide complex tachycardia with atypical left bundle branch morphology
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Inferior axis on ECG
Post-treatment ECG showed normal sinus rhythm at 64 bpm
Precordial T-wave inversion in leads V1 to V5, I, and aVL on post-treatment ECG
Epsilon wave present in lead V4 on post-treatment ECG
Low voltage in limb leads on post-treatment ECG
Echocardiography showed global hypokinesia of right ventricle and dilated RV
Cardiac MRI showed grossly dilated RV, high RV end diastolic volume, and low RV ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG and imaging findings consistent with ARVC, including epsilon wave and grossly dilated RV

shortlist.label: Ventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Wide complex tachycardia on ECG, consistent with VT

shortlist.label: Brugada Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings, including atypical left bundle branch morphology and inferior axis, suggestive of Brugada Syndrome

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Intermittent palpitations and wide complex tachycardia, consistent with CPVT

shortlist.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: ECG and imaging findings, including dilated RVOT, consistent with RVOT tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG and imaging studies are consistent with ARVC, including epsilon waves, T-wave inversion, and low voltage in limb leads on ECG, as well as global hypokinesia and dilatation of the right ventricle on echocardiography and cardiac MRI.

rejected.label: Ventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient presented with wide complex tachycardia, the underlying structural and functional abnormalities of the right ventricle suggest a more specific diagnosis of ARVC.

rejected.label: Brugada Syndrome
rejected.why: Although Brugada Syndrome can present with similar ECG findings, the patient's cardiac MRI and echocardiography results are more consistent with ARVC.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is not seen in this patient's ECG studies.

rejected.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient's ECG shows a wide complex tachycardia, the imaging studies suggest a more extensive involvement of the right ventricle, consistent with ARVC.
